name: osd-vscode
description: ABAP Unit in the Test Explorer, the serving generation and short dumps of a running osd

osd.url.description: The listener of a running osd (npm start, build/osd up). Set automatically to the launched instance's own address while B0 (osd.start) is running one.

osd.home.description: B0 (docs/vscode-extension.md, "B0 spike"): the open-steamgate checkout osd.start builds and runs. Empty uses the workspace folder when the window has exactly one.

osd.keymap.description: What an ABAP developer's fingers expect (SAP GUI / ADT: Ctrl+F2 Check, Ctrl+F3 Activate, F8 Run, the debug keys) over an .abap editor, or VS Code's own bindings unchanged ("vscode").

osd.notebook.rowLimit.description: The row limit (rowNumber) a *.osdnb cell's SELECT is run with, against /sap/bc/adt/datapreview/freestyle.

osd.dataPreview.rowLimit.description: The row limit (rowNumber) F8's Data Preview on a TABL or a DDLS is run with, against /sap/bc/adt/datapreview/ddic or /cds.

osd.hotspots.refreshSeconds.description: How often the ZOSD_DUMP heat (line decorations, explorer badges) is re-read. 0 turns the timer off; osd.run, osd.activate and "osd: Refresh hotspots" still refresh it.

osd.tests.showSystem.description: Whether the Test Explorer's System group (the libraries abap_transpile.json's own "libs" pull in -- open-abap-core, abapgit, ... -- shown collapsed) is built at all. Off hides it and skips scanning those folders.

osd.openIn.description: Where a click on a Services tree row (App, ICF, OData) opens it: the system browser (vscode.env.openExternal), or a webview tab inside VS Code (an iframe of the running osd's own URL, the way the SEGW editor's and the gui-reports spike's own panels do it). APC rows have no default click either way -- a WebSocket URL does nothing opened as a page.

osd.database.system.description: What osd.start runs the system on (test/setup.mjs's own STG_DB). A password never lives here -- "osd: Set database password (HANA)" / "(PostgreSQL)" store it in VS Code's own secret storage. duckdb needs the native module (@duckdb/node-api): not available in a packaged install.

osd.database.tests.description: What a Test Explorer run (or osd.run's own detached run) uses, when it should be a DIFFERENT database than osd.database.system -- e.g. the live system on sqlite while tests run on a real hana. "same" (the default) sends no override at all.

osd.database.postgres.host.description: PostgreSQL host for osd.database.system/tests = postgres. Empty uses the client's own default (PGHOST, else "postgres").

osd.database.postgres.port.description: PostgreSQL port. 0 uses the client's own default (PGPORT, else 5432).

osd.database.postgres.user.description: PostgreSQL user. Empty uses the client's own default (PGUSER, else "osd").

osd.database.postgres.database.description: PostgreSQL database -- the isolation boundary (tools/postgres-client.mjs never drops or rewrites a pre-existing schema). Empty defaults to a dedicated osd_<hash> derived from osd.home, so this window never writes into somebody else's database by accident.

osd.database.hana.host.description: HANA host for osd.database.system/tests = hana. Empty uses the client's own default (HANA_HOST/HXE_HOST, else "localhost").

osd.database.hana.port.description: HANA port. 0 uses the client's own default (HANA_PORT/HXE_PORT, else 39017).

osd.database.hana.user.description: HANA user. Empty uses the client's own default (HANA_USER/HXE_USER, else "SYSTEM").

osd.database.hana.schema.description: HANA schema -- the isolation boundary. Empty defaults to a dedicated OSD_<HASH> derived from osd.home, so this window never writes into an existing schema by accident.

osd.database.hana.fresh.description: STG_DB_FRESH=1: drop and rebuild osd.database.hana.schema on the next start instead of refusing a schema this build did not stamp. osd.start turns this on itself (and asks first) when a start fails with that refusal.
